newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Some basis offers move higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Some basis offers move higher.

text.p: Some soymeal basis offers in rail and truck markets were higher on Friday in response to an expected slowdown in production at some Illinois and Indiana crushing plants this weekend, cash brokers said.
"We've been crushing too much, so people are finally looking at some downtime," a dealer in the southeast said.
Supplies of unsold soymeal have been heavy this week, and that buildup has prompted the downtime, dealers said.
The National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush of 23.014 million bushels was more than one million bushels below last week's crush and well below trade expectations.
Estimates for the National Oilseed Processor Associations' weekly crush had ranged from 23.50 million to 24.50 million bushels.
There was also talk of an unspecified quantity of meal sold for export. That talked also helped firm up basis in some Illinois markets, dealers said.
In export news, South Korea passed on a tender for 40,000 tonnes of soymeal for September/October arrival. The tender has been rescheduled for Tuesday.
